title: October | 2026 | FRED Blog
gist: BEA data show 44 of 50 US states plus DC grew in Q2 2026 (national 2.2% annualized) but growth was top-heavy: the median state grew 1.7% and 32 states lagged, with finance-led New York (4%) leading and mining-heavy West Virginia (-2.3%) and Wyoming contracting. Q1 revisions averaged about +/-2 points, flipping Alaska from +2.8% to -3.8%.

insights.claim: In Q2 2026, 44 of 50 US state economies plus Washington, DC grew, with national real GDP growth averaging 2.2% annualized per BEA data released September 30, 2026.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Broad-based expansion in Q2 2026 argues against an imminent nationwide recession.
insights.quote: 44 of 50 state economies plus Washington, DC, grew in the second quarter. The national average was at 2.2% annualized growth.

insights.claim: US Q2 2026 growth was top-heavy: the median state (Iowa) grew only 1.7% annualized versus the 2.2% national average, and 32 states grew slower than the national rate.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Headline GDP overstates the typical regional economy; growth is concentrated in a few large states.
insights.quote: The median state, Iowa, grew at 1.7%, which is below the national average. 32 states had slower growth than the national average.

insights.claim: New York posted the fastest Q2 2026 state real GDP growth at 4% annualized, followed by South Carolina and Delaware at 3.5%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Leadership by NY and DE points to finance-driven rather than broad industrial growth.
insights.quote: New York had the fastest annualized growth, at 4%. South Carolina and Delaware were next, at 3.5% growth.

insights.claim: All eight states in the St. Louis Fed's Eighth District grew in Q2 2026 but every one grew slower than the national average, with Mississippi and Illinois leading at 2.1%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Midwest/South-central regional economies are lagging the national pace.
insights.quote: The St. Louis Fed’s Eighth District states grew in the second quarter, with all eight growing slower than the national average.
insights.locator: The St. Louis Fed’s Eighth District

themes.theme: Sector drivers: finance up, mining down

insights.claim: Per the BEA, finance and insurance were the leading contributors to Q2 2026 real GDP growth in New York and Delaware, the top-performing states.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Financial-sector strength is the main engine of the fastest-growing state economies, implying sensitivity to market conditions.
insights.quote: finance and insurance sectors were the leading contributors to the increase in real GDP in New York and Delaware
insights.locator: According to the BEA press release

insights.claim: Six energy/commodity-heavy states contracted in Q2 2026 (Alaska, Kansas, Nebraska, North Dakota, West Virginia, Wyoming), with West Virginia worst at -2.3% and Wyoming at -1.6%, and mining was the leading drag in West Virginia and Wyoming.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: The contraction cluster in mining/energy and farm states signals weak commodity/extractive activity in Q2 2026.
insights.quote: Mining was the leading contributor to the decline in West Virginia and Wyoming.

themes.theme: Revision risk in state GDP data

insights.claim: Q1 2026 state GDP growth revisions averaged roughly +/-2 percentage points across states and DC, meaning initial state prints are highly unreliable.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Treat first-release state GDP as noisy; avoid over-reading single-quarter regional moves.
insights.quote: Q1 revisions averaged  +/- 2% across all states and Washington, DC.

insights.claim: Alaska's Q1 2026 growth was revised from +2.8% to -3.8% (largest downward revision) while Washington, DC was revised from 2.2% to 7.3% (largest upward), showing revisions can flip the sign of growth.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Revisions can swing a state from expansion to contraction, so ALFRED vintage data matter for backtesting.
insights.quote: The largest downward revision was for Alaska: from 2.8% to -3.8%.

insights.claim: State GDP data are subject to an annual revision the following March, and the ALFRED database preserves data vintages so users can see figures as originally published.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Use ALFRED vintages to avoid look-ahead bias when modeling with regional GDP.
